text: Ux-Vakka, the tag-keeper at the Tag House, told me White Rose Prison holds the graves of Argonians who died mid-Owing, far from their Hist. The Chainbreakers carry such bones home. I'm to ask Okan-Sei, who carries for the villages.
Okan-Sei told me the White Rose bones are carried from White Rose Prison.
Ux-Vakka or Okan-Sei has died at the Tag House. The White Rose bones will not be carried from the Tag House now.

Gnaeus Martius, serjeant of the Broke Column, asked me for the column's levy. Gideon's governor will not pay to clear the column. The toll company's officers want to use the column themselves. I mean to clear the camp myself.
The Broke Column camp is cleared. No levy is taken on the track below it now.

The headwoman at the Shrine of Haynekhtnamet told me four villages bring offerings to the shrine each wet season. This year is her village's turn. The flooding got worse. Coin is no use on the offering shelf. I'm to bring her river salt to lay on it.
The headwoman at the Shrine of Haynekhtnamet asked me for river salt to lay on the offering shelf. I have the salt. I must tell her the shelf is laid.
I laid river salt on the offering shelf at the Shrine of Haynekhtnamet, among older offerings corroding where they lie. The headwoman says her village's turn is kept for this wet season.
The headwoman at the Shrine of Haynekhtnamet is dead. Her village's offering will not be laid this wet season.
Gnaeus Martius, serjeant of the Broke Column, told me the column would disband if Gideon offered a pardon and a wage. I'm to hear the column's terms from the serjeant below the camp.
The column's terms are a pardon and a wage. Gideon is the one who can give them. I'm to carry the terms to Gideon.
Gnaeus Martius is dead. I cannot learn the column's terms now.
Prices-The-Salvage told me the diggers at the Bog Iron Workings have left the deep end of the seep. I'm to look past the deep end myself.
Past the deep end of the seep I found the den of a giant leech. I'm to tell Meets-Every-Tide what I found.
The diggers come from three villages. I'm to carry word of the den to Swampmoth Town, below a fort on firm ground.

Livia Varinius keeps the well at Claywater Station. She told me the well and the landing each charge a traveller for the same stop. I'm to cross the ford and ask Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, what the landing charges for its half.

Livia Varinius sent me across the ford at Claywater Station to ask about the two charges. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me the landing is older than the well and will not help to mend it in stone. His people gave up building in stone long ago; they build in mud and timber. I must carry the landing's terms back to Livia Varinius.

I carried the landing's terms back to Livia Varinius at Claywater Station. Signs-For-The-Cargo will not help to mend the well in stone. Livia Varinius will take the matter of the two charges up with him in person.
One of the two keepers at Claywater Station is dead. The well's charge and the landing's charge were never settled.

Reeh-Shaal, a traveller at Greenspring bound for Helstrom, told me the city spring at Helstrom runs sour on a cycle. The assembly will not time the cycle in open session. I'm to ask Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, how she tells when water is turning.

Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, told me salt is reaching her spring from upstream. Reeh-Shaal says the city spring at Helstrom runs sour on a cycle. To learn the cycle I must ask in Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal the traveller or Im-Moro the spring-keeper has died at Greenspring. I will learn nothing more of the sour water at Helstrom from Greenspring.

Haj-Tei, the bed-keeper at Greenspring, told me two convocation delegations sleep in his beds rather than pay pitch rent at Nine-Trunks. They want the use of the spring written down before the next convocation. I'm to ask Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, on what terms the spring is kept.

Haj-Tei, the bed-keeper at Greenspring, asked me to learn the terms of the spring for two convocation delegations. Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, told me the tribe charges nothing for the water. I'm to ask Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal to set the terms down.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal set down the terms of the spring at Greenspring at my asking. The tribe charges nothing for the water. Beds and rope cost coin. The delegations will carry the terms to the convocation at Nine-Trunks.
Haj-Tei the bed-keeper, Im-Moro the spring-keeper or Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring has died before the terms were set. The terms of the spring will not be written down for the delegations.

Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, told me a body was lifted out of the spring. The whole interior drinks that water without boiling it. Two households at the spring would rather it went unspoken. I'm to ask Mee-Sei and Tsono-Ra of the spring families what they saw.

Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, asked me to hear the spring families about the body lifted out of the spring. Mee-Sei and Tsono-Ra have both answered me. I must tell Im-Moro what the households said.
I told Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, what Mee-Sei and Tsono-Ra said about the body in the spring. She will say it aloud now, whatever the households would prefer.
Im-Moro the spring-keeper, Mee-Sei or Tsono-Ra of Greenspring has died before the matter was settled. The body in the spring will go unspoken now.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring told me Nine-Trunks rents convocation pitch at a high rate. Two delegations have camped at Greenspring instead. I'm to ask Haj-Tei, the bed-keeper, what the delegations pay for his beds.

Haj-Tei, the bed-keeper at Greenspring, told me beds there cost a great deal. The delegations still pay for the beds, but they do not pay the pitch rent at Nine-Trunks. I must take the pitch rent to Nine-Trunks itself.
Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal or Haj-Tei the bed-keeper of Greenspring has died. The pitch rent at Nine-Trunks will not be taken up from Greenspring now.

Xuth-Ozzu, a Root Steward of Hissmir at Greenspring, told me the Trials of the Burnished Scales let one without a Hist commune with the Hist. A Root Steward cannot refuse a comer, so Xuth-Ozzu gives the trial at Greenspring. I'm to ask Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, for leave to stand before the Greenspring Hist.
Vees-Wai, the tree-minder at Greenspring, gave me leave to stand before the Hist once I had tasted the water of the pool beneath it. I must go back to Xuth-Ozzu, the Root Steward of Hissmir.
I stood before the Hist at Greenspring for Xuth-Ozzu's Trial of the Burnished Scales. The Hist let me hear it.
Xuth-Ozzu the Root Steward or Vees-Wai the tree-minder has died at Greenspring. The Trial of the Burnished Scales will not be given to me there now.

Opens-The-Books speaks for the Lighter Flotilla. She told me the Lilmoth council wants every lighter licensed. The last time it tried, the crews stopped the port for two weeks. I'm to ask Xal-Jei what terms the crews would take.
Xal-Jei gave me the crews' terms. If the council opens the tariff, the crews will talk about a licence. I must carry them to the council in Lilmoth.
One of the two I was to speak with on the flotilla is dead.

Xal-Jei, master of a lighter, told me some cargo comes ashore at night and never touches the quay. It is settled at the dice tables. I'm to ask Reeh-Tei, who mends nets on the flotilla, what comes past at night.
Reeh-Tei told me where the night cargo is settled: at the dice tables on the Outside Barge.
One of the two who spoke of the night cargo is dead. I can learn no more of the night cargo.
Sells-The-Last-Sack sells salvage at Chasepoint. She told me this week's lot came off a ship whose owners do not know it sank. I'm to ask Aelia Nerva, the station-keeper, who ought to be told.
Aelia Nerva heard me out about the salvage lot at Chasepoint. Whoever owned that ship will be found in Soulrest, west along the coast road.
Aelia Nerva is dead. The ship's owners will not hear of their loss through me.

Aelia Nerva told me a road survey went out east of Soulrest to price a causeway repair. Then its word stopped coming back. Chasepoint is the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland. I'm to walk to The Tag House on the Prison road and look for the survey's trail.
I reached The Tag House, on its dry rise beside the Prison road. The survey's road runs on toward White-Rose Prison.
Aelia Nerva is dead. The road survey was her concern.

Aelia Nerva keeps the road stage at Chasepoint. She told me no keeper there has been paid in two centuries. Two families each claim the office. I'm to hear Argues-With-The-Clerk out for one of the families.
Argues-With-The-Clerk told me his family's claim to the keeper's office at Chasepoint. The other family is at the Fourth Stage, further along the coast road.
One of the two claimants at Chasepoint is dead. I cannot settle which family holds the keeper's office.

Sells-The-Last-Sack told me the wreckers who pull people off the bar keep them as salvage crew, to work off the cost of their own rescue. I'm to ask Opens-The-Second-Shed at Chasepoint what that rescue costs.
Opens-The-Second-Shed told me what a rescue off the bar costs. The crews who are working it off are with the wreckers of the Long Bar.
One of the two who spoke of the salvage crews at Chasepoint is dead. I will learn no more there.

Heita-Kai, lieutenant of the North Cut Camp, told me the camp's men take payment each season to keep the track quiet. Long-Water Hold has begun paying it. I'm to ask Heita-Kai at the bend of the track about the camp's receipts.
Heita-Kai told me the camp's men cut a tally-stick as a receipt for each payment. Long-Water Hold keeps its own accounts. That is my next stop.
Heita-Kai is dead. I cannot learn more about the North Cut Camp's payments now.
Bux-Neel mends nets at Nine Bends. He told me the village's fish traps stand where the free port's boats now load. I'm to ask Deeka-Seesh, the village elder, whether the village will argue for them.
Deeka-Seesh told me both claims are old enough that each side can argue its case: the village's traps and the port's right to load there. The traps stand at Alten Corimont, nine bends downriver.
Deeka-Seesh is dead. The village has no elder to argue its claim to the traps.
Deeka-Seesh, the elder at Nine Bends, told me the same cut mark shows at the waterline on each of the nine bends. One is at the village landing. I'm to go and look at it.
I found the cut mark at the waterline beside the Nine Bends landing. I should tell Deeka-Seesh.
I told Deeka-Seesh I had seen the mark. She said the village stopped counting the marks a generation ago.
Deeka-Seesh is dead. I can tell her nothing of the mark at the landing now.

Swims-The-Channel-Twice minds the tree at Nine Bends. She told me the refuge downriver has a clutch to name and no Hist of its own. The village has offered to do the naming. I'm to ask Deeka-Seesh, the elder.
Deeka-Seesh told me a naming needs the Hist and its hatchery pool. The camp that keeps the clutch is a day downriver of the tree.
Deeka-Seesh is dead. I cannot ask her about the naming now.
Gnaeus Martius, serjeant of the Broke Column, told me the column's men stand a watch over the Gideon road. I'm to ask the serjeant below the camp which boats the watch counts.
Gnaeus Martius told me the watch counts the boats by the toll office's own published schedules. The toll office is at Cartwright's Cross. That is my next stop.
Gnaeus Martius is dead. I cannot learn which boats the watch counts now.
Aelia Nerva told me a wreck has come in on the bar south of Chasepoint. The salvage families will not work it. Buys-Cheap has been out to look. I'm to ask him what is aboard.
Buys-Cheap told me what he saw aboard the wreck. The wreckers of the Long Bar have it now.
One of the two who knew about the wreck at Chasepoint is dead. I will hear no more of it there.

Ux-Vakka, the tag-keeper at the Tag House, gave me a bone-tag that came back from the villages for a woman of the Rose. Her family were told she walked out years ago. I'm to take the tag to Vees-Kai of that family, who waits under the shelter.
I gave Vees-Kai the bone-tag. Her family were told the woman walked out of the Rose, but if a tag comes back, there are bones behind it. I'm to learn in the Rose what became of her.
Vees-Kai has died at the Tag House. The bone-tag cannot reach her family from here now.

Okan-Sei, the villages' carrier at the Tag House, told me a trafficker moves living people out of the Rose on the papers of the dead. Every carriage charge is written in the tag-keeper's book, in his hut.
I read in the charge book that Tag 17 was released after a week with no name given. The Chainbreakers paid forty drakes for it.
Ux-Vakka could not say whose bones went out as Tag 17. A living person may have left the Rose under that charge.
Ux-Vakka or Okan-Sei has died at the Tag House. I can learn nothing more here about the papers of the dead.

Ux-Vakka, the tag-keeper at the Tag House, told me some of the tags on his wall are hung for people who are still alive. He did not hang them. I'm to ask Sal-Ozzu, who waits under the shelter, whose names they carry.
Sal-Ozzu told me the names on the living tags belong to families in Vaunting. I'm to learn in Vaunting who hung them.
Ux-Vakka or Sal-Ozzu has died at the Tag House. I will learn nothing more here of the tags that hang for living people.

Lifts-Two-Traps keeps the toll post at Riverwalk. Thorn and Hissmir both claim the toll on the pilgrim water. Paying either one counts as taking that side. I'm to ask Deesh-Ra, the stage-mistress, what she makes of the two claims.
Deesh-Ra told me Riverwalk's people earn their living from the ferry stage and the toll. I'm to carry her word back to Lifts-Two-Traps.
I gave Lifts-Two-Traps the stage-mistress's word. Thorn and Hissmir still both claim the toll.
Lifts-Two-Traps or Deesh-Ra is dead. The two claims at Riverwalk are closed to me now.
The toll at Riverwalk is argued over every night. Reaches-The-Shore-Last, a toll hand, told me last night's argument ended in an accusation. I'm to ask Lifts-Two-Traps, the toll-holder, about it.
Lifts-Two-Traps told me a witness can prove the accusation. The witness is at the Pilots' Rest. That is my next stop.
Lifts-Two-Traps is dead. The accusation cannot be proved now.
Half-Tail of the boat crew at Riverwalk told me the way across the cove silted up overnight. Boats will pass Riverwalk by if it stays silted. I'm to ask Deesh-Ra, the stage-mistress, about it.
Deesh-Ra told me the villagers sound the way across the cove every morning. I'm to ask Runs-The-Line-Out, a toll hand, about sounding it again.
Runs-The-Line-Out sounded the way across the cove again. Boats can reach the ferry stage.
Deesh-Ra or Runs-The-Line-Out is dead. The way across the cove was never sounded again. The cove stays silted.

Vees-Wai, the tree-minder at Greenspring, told me the village's Hist has begun to sicken. The village blames salt from the works upstream. I'm to ask Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, what the water tells her.

Im-Moro, the spring-keeper at Greenspring, told me salt is reaching the spring. The village blames the salt works upstream. Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, says the sick Hist is judged below its roots, in the drowned galleries under the village.
Vees-Wai the tree-minder or Im-Moro the spring-keeper has died at Greenspring. The sick Hist's roots are closed to me now.

Ohl-Nakka, the nisswo of the Teeth of Sithis, meets each pilgrim at the last bend of the pilgrim water and asks what offering they bring. He took mine. The Clutch of Nisswo will accept me. He spoke of a faction that claims to have found the temple's lost first purpose. I'm to hear the rest from him at the last bend.
Ohl-Nakka sent me into the temple with word of the claim. I'm to give it to Zaxi-Rekh, a priest of the Teeth.
I gave Zaxi-Rekh word of the claim. The Clutch accept that the temple's first purpose is lost. They teach the loss to pilgrims.
Ohl-Nakka or Zaxi-Rekh is dead. I cannot learn more about the claim at the Teeth of Sithis now.
Deeka-Kaya, the surface tender at the Counted Lots, told me a diver came up dead on lot four. She had no right to work that lot. I'm to ask Ohl-Jei, who dives beside it.
Ohl-Jei told me lot four was never the dead diver's. Lots pass by inheritance. Disputes over them are settled in Archon.
Deeka-Kaya or Ohl-Jei has died at the Counted Lots. I will learn nothing more here of the death on lot four.

Deeka-Kaya, the surface tender at the Counted Lots, told me a lot has outlived its last heir and four families dive it to stake a claim. A claimant must pay the heirs' line a share of the lot's worth, so the worth must be set first. A drowned diver's basket lies eight metres down by the fourth lot.
I brought up the deep-lot pearl from the drowned diver's basket. Deeka-Kaya wants to see it.
Deeka-Kaya took the deep-lot pearl to set the heirs' share. The claim on the heirless lot is settled in Archon.
Deeka-Kaya has died at the Counted Lots. The heirless lot will not be valued at the Counted Lots now.
Bones lie outside a cave mouth among the roots at Takes-The-Tools, with old tools among them. Something has made a lair of the hollow.
I cleared the lair at Takes-The-Tools. The hiring camp a kilometre east can forage twice as far. Its overseers pay in goods.
Ninx-Ossa keeps the purse for the Lighter Flotilla. She told me the speaker keeps a tally of cargo off a hull that never reached the quay. She wants the list. I must take it unseen.
I took the list unseen. I must bring it to Ninx-Ossa.
I gave Ninx-Ossa the list. Now she knows what the hidden cache holds.
I was seen taking the list. Ninx-Ossa will not deal with me again.
Ninx-Ossa is dead.

Clear the Broke Column camp

Tell Meets-Every-Tide about the leech den
Kill the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford.
Bring the landing's clay basket back from the cut.
Hear Signs-For-The-Cargo's side, and what ails the landing, at the raft.
Hear Livia Varinius's side at the well.
Find out whether the well has cracked before.
Put terms to Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo before the rains.
Find out why the well at Claywater Station keeps failing.

Ask Tsono-Ra about the body in the spring
Tell Im-Moro what the households said
Ask Haj-Tei what the delegations pay for beds
Ask Vees-Wai for leave to stand before the Hist
Return to Xuth-Ozzu
Ask Xal-Jei what terms the crews would take
Ask Reeh-Tei what comes past the flotilla at night
Ask Aelia Nerva who owns the sunk ship
Walk to The Tag House on the Prison road
Hear Argues-With-The-Clerk's claim to the keeper's office
Ask Opens-The-Second-Shed what a rescue off the bar costs
Ask Heita-Kai about the camp's receipts at the bend of the track
Ask Deeka-Seesh about the traps on the ninth bend
Find the cut mark at the waterline by the landing
Tell Deeka-Seesh about the mark at the landing
Ask Deeka-Seesh about the naming
Ask Gnaeus Martius below the camp which boats the watch counts
Ask Buys-Cheap what is aboard the wreck
Take the bone-tag to Vees-Kai under the shelter
Ask Ux-Vakka about Tag 17
Read the carriage charge book in the tag-keeper's hut
Ask Sal-Ozzu whose names the tags carry
Ask Deesh-Ra, the stage-mistress, about the two claims on the toll
Take Deesh-Ra's word back to Lifts-Two-Traps at the toll post
Ask Lifts-Two-Traps about the accusation
Ask Runs-The-Line-Out about the sounded way
Ask Deesh-Ra about the silted cove
Ask Im-Moro what the spring water tells her
Ask Zaxi-Rekh about the claim on the temple
Hear Ohl-Nakka out about the claimed purpose
Ask Ohl-Jei about the death on lot four
Show Deeka-Kaya the deep-lot pearl
Dive to the drowned diver's basket by the fourth lot and take the deep-lot pearl

Give the hull tally to Ninx-Ossa
